serviceIdentification.serviceDescription: VisualVault is a secure, scalable platform that helps government agencies automate constituent-facing processes that require Compliance and Enforcement — from licensing and permitting to case management and general compliance enforcement. It enables agencies to configure workflows and adapt to evolving requirements.

trustCenter.repositoryDescription: VisualVault Cloud FedRAMP Trust Center. Publishes compliance programs, controls, third-party interconnections, and package deliverables.

additionalRepositories.repositoryDescription: VisualVault information security policies and procedures, each governing one or more NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls.
additionalRepositories.accessRequestInstructions: Contact fedramp-security@visualvault.com to request access to policy documents.

assessor.name: A-LIGN Compliance and Security, Inc. dba A-LIGN

certified.useCase: AWS GovCloud (US) hosts VisualVault Cloud's infrastructure for the government-exclusive offering.
Microsoft Entra ID (via Azure Government) provides internal corporate single sign-on for personnel accessing VisualVault Cloud.

CrowdStrike Falcon Platform for Government provides endpoint detection and response across VisualVault's corporate AWS and AWS GovCloud infrastructure, via separate subscriptions for each environment.
KnowBe4 Platform provides security awareness training for VisualVault personnel.

relevantPolicies.name: Physical and Environmental Protection Policy (POLICY-0010)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for physical access and environmental protection of information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 (Moderate) controls. It covers infrastructure hosting requirements (requiring a FedRAMP Moderate authorized IaaS provider such as AWS), alternate work site security controls for remote staff, and approval requirements for delivery/removal of information systems from facilities.

relevantPolicies.name: Vendor Management Policy
relevantPolicies.fileName: (SR-01) Supply Chain and Vendor Risk Management Policy.pdf
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for ensuring third-party vendors and cloud service providers protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of company and customer data. It covers vendor risk assessment and inventory, required contract security clauses (including for cloud and telecom providers), and change management for vendor services. The policy is based on NIST 800-53 controls.

relevantPolicies.name: VisualVault Audit and Accountability Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy (POLICY-0013) establishes VisualVault's requirements for audit and accountability controls based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) and NIST SP 800-92 guidelines. It covers audit scope and independence, required loggable events and metadata, response to audit failures, time synchronization, log review/analysis, protection and retention of audit records, and role-based access to audit data. It also defines enforcement measures for policy violations and documents review/approval history.

relevantPolicies.name: Access, Identification, and Authentication Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for controlling access, identification, and authentication to its information systems, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers topics such as least privilege access, user registration, role-based access control, terminal and account protection, separation of duties, network access control, external system use, and multi-factor authentication.

relevantPolicies.name: Media Protection Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for handling digital and non-digital media, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It covers media access authorization, marking, storage, transport (including encryption), and sanitization/disposal procedures, along with roles, responsibilities, and enforcement provisions.

relevantPolicies.name: Personnel Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for managing personnel, including responsibilities for policy oversight, employee acknowledgment, and a tiered corrective action/sanctions framework for security and confidentiality violations. It is based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4 (Moderate) controls, covering all VisualVault personnel and third parties using VisualVault systems.

relevantPolicies.name: Configuration Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for configuring, monitoring, and maintaining its information systems in accordance with NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (Moderate) controls. It covers baseline configurations, change control, configuration settings, least functionality, system component inventory, software usage restrictions, and firewall requirements. It also defines roles and responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, third parties, and customers.

relevantPolicies.name: Risk Assessment Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes requirements for risk assessment and vulnerability management based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls. It defines responsibilities for management and the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, security categorization, risk assessment frequency, vulnerability scanning schedules, remediation timelines by severity, and reporting requirements to FedRAMP officials. It also outlines enforcement measures for non-compliance.

relevantPolicies.name: Mobile Device Policy (POLICY-0003)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's security requirements for mobile device usage, covering laptops, portable devices (tablets/smartphones), and BYOD/POCD scenarios. It defines device classification, required security controls (authentication, encryption, remote wipe), Wi-Fi/AP security practices, and personnel responsibilities based on NIST SP 800-124 guidance.

relevantPolicies.name: SOP-0030 - Information Release
relevantPolicies.summary: This procedure establishes controls to prevent unintended disclosure or spillage of information when VisualVault personnel release content to publicly accessible systems such as the website, status page, or help site. It defines authorized personnel, review and approval steps, special handling for sensitive/confidential information (including NDA and redaction requirements), and a quarterly review process for authorized posting locations.

relevantPolicies.name: Operations Management Policy
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy defines requirements for IT operations security based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering system maintenance, systems and communications protection, and system/information integrity. It outlines responsibilities for management, the Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties, and specifies technical controls such as maintenance procedures, boundary protection, encryption, malicious code protection, and system monitoring.

relevantPolicies.name: Contingency Planning Policy (POLICY-0004)
relevantPolicies.summary: This policy establishes VisualVault's requirements for contingency planning, based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, to ensure the organization can maintain and restore availability of its information systems after a disruption. It covers development, distribution, training, and testing of the Disaster Recovery/Business Continuity Plan, along with information system backup, data retention schedules, and periodic data restoration testing.

relevantPolicies.name: Information Security Policy (POLICY-0009)
relevantPolicies.summary: This VisualVault policy establishes the organization's information security program based on NIST SP 800-53 Rev 4 (Moderate) controls, covering security awareness training (SETA), incident response and information spillage handling, and security planning including the system security plan and information security architecture. It defines roles and responsibilities across the Security Team, Director of Cybersecurity and Compliance, personnel, and third parties, and outlines enforcement and annual review requirements.
